title: Time Reaper — The *Consume Anomaly* effect doesn't appear to work.
scope: Time Reaper Consume Anomaly trigger: P1 exiles own Memnite face-up via Swords to Plowshares; P0 casts Time Reaper, attacks P1 (haste), P1 blocks nothing; trigger target selection exercised; native engine, P0 + P1 human driver seats, protocol-98 driver
result: A1 setup passed (P1 exile holds a face-up Memnite; P0 ready to cast Time Reaper). A2 passed: after 4 combat damage, the Consume Anomaly trigger went on the stack and P0 received a TriggerTargetSelection prompt (sequence, choose 1). A3 FAILED (the reported outcome): the prompt offered exactly 2 candidates, both players (seats 0 and 1) - the face-up exiled Memnite was not offered, so the reported 'would only let me target an opponent' reproduces exactly. A4 failed as the flip side (players offered). A5: taking the only legal target (P1), the trigger resolved with the Memnite still in exile and P1's library unchanged, yet P0 gained 3 life (20->23) - the 'if you do' clause fired although no card moved. Matches the triage: the PutAtLibraryPosition target is parsed as unfiltered 'any', so the selector falls back to offering players.

limitations: Browser UI not exercised; native engine via two human driver seats.
Dense playsets (8x Time Reaper, 16x Memnite, 8x Swords) are a test-harness convenience (engine accepts >4-of for custom games).

The Swords-to-Plowshares self-exile used the engine's single-candidate auto-target path (cast with the Memnite as the only creature on the battlefield); manual target prompting for Swords was not exercised.
Only the 'target the offered player' follow-through was exercised; the reporter's session presumably did the same. No decline/alternative branch exists (the trigger is not optional).
States are authoritative exports, restorable only via full game replay (driver/scenario_7349.py), not direct load.
Not tested on the report's original build (Discord report, 2026-08-13); verdict scoped to v0.99.0, not a fix claim.
